claims.text: Reference dependence can play a major role in the effectiveness of default effects.
Queries formulated by defaults can produce differences in constructed preferences.
Manipulating queries can mitigate default effects.

evidence.description: In three experiments we produce default effects and demonstrate that reference dependence can play a major role in their effectiveness.
We find that the queries formulated by defaults can produce differences in constructed preferences
further that manipulating queries can also mitigate default effects.

methodologies.name: Consumer choice experiment manipulating defaults and queries
methodologies.description: Three experimental studies evaluating choices between incandescent and compact fluorescent bulbs while measuring rationales including effort, implied endorsement, and reference dependence.

limitations.text: Reference dependence as an explanation for default effects has received far less empirical attention in past research compared to effort and implied endorsement.
